# Google Drive integration (`pyrunner_integrations.google_drive`)

Google Drive for scripts: list, upload and download files, make folders and share links.

Files come back in Drive's own shape, with these fields unless you ask for
others: `id`, `name`, `mimeType`, `parents`, `size` (bytes, as text;
none for Google Docs, Sheets and Slides), `modifiedTime` and
`webViewLink`. A file's or folder's id is the part of its URL after
`/d/` or `/folders/`. Files in shared drives work too.

The connection is a Google connection with a Drive scope set: **Drive: files
it made or opened** (`drive.file`) sees only the files this connection
uploaded or created; **Drive: all files** (`drive`) sees everything the
account can. Its token goes only to `https://www.googleapis.com`.

## Connection

It uses a connection of the **Google** kind (provider `google`), which signs in with OAuth (Connect or a pasted token). Add one under **Connections** in the sidebar and grant it to the script. Every function takes `connection=`: the connection's name, or nothing for the script's one `google` connection.

The credentials go only to the connection's base URL; a redirect elsewhere goes on without them.

## Example

```python
from pyrunner_integrations import google_drive

# Upload today's report into a folder and get a link anyone can open.
folder = google_drive.create_folder("Reports")
uploaded = google_drive.upload("/tmp/report.pdf", folder=folder["id"])
print(google_drive.share_link(uploaded["id"]))

# The ten most recent PDFs, then download the first one.
pdfs = list(google_drive.list_files(query="mimeType = 'application/pdf'", order_by="modifiedTime desc", limit=10))
if pdfs:
    google_drive.download(pdfs[0]["id"], "/tmp/latest.pdf")
```

## Functions

### list_files

```python
google_drive.list_files(*, query=None, folder=None, fields=None, order_by=None, include_trashed=False, limit=None, connection=None)
```

Yield the files the connection can see, fetching pages as it goes.

`folder` limits it to one folder's direct children (the folder's id).
`query` is a Drive search query of your own
(`"name contains 'invoice' and mimeType = 'application/pdf'"`). Trashed
files are left out unless `include_trashed`. `fields` replaces the
default file fields, `order_by` sorts (`"modifiedTime desc"`),
`limit` stops after that many. For example:

```python
for f in google_drive.list_files(folder=folder_id, order_by="modifiedTime desc", limit=20):
    print(f["name"], f["modifiedTime"])
```

### get_file

```python
google_drive.get_file(file_id, *, fields=None, connection=None)
```

One file's (or folder's) details; one that doesn't exist (or isn't visible) raises NOT_FOUND.

For example:

```python
info = google_drive.get_file(file_id)
print(info["name"], info["mimeType"])
```

### create_folder

```python
google_drive.create_folder(name, *, parent=None, connection=None)
```

Create a folder (in `parent`, a folder's id, or at the top of My Drive); returns it.

For example:

```python
folder = google_drive.create_folder("Reports 2026")
google_drive.upload("report.pdf", folder=folder["id"])
```

### upload

```python
google_drive.upload(source, *, name=None, folder=None, mime_type=None, file_id=None, connection=None)
```

Upload a file; returns the new file.

`source` is a file's path, or the content as bytes (then `name` is
needed; for text, `text.encode()`). `name` defaults to the path's file
name, `mime_type` to a guess from the name. `folder` puts it in that
folder (its id). `file_id` replaces that file's content instead (and its
name, when `name` is given; pass `mime_type` when replacing with bytes
and no name). The content is read into memory; files over 5 MB go as a
resumable upload, in one request. For example:

```python
uploaded = google_drive.upload("/tmp/report.pdf", folder=folder_id)
google_drive.upload(b"id,total\n1,30\n", name="totals.csv", folder=folder_id)
```

### download

```python
google_drive.download(file_id, path=None, *, export_as=None, connection=None)
```

A file's content: bytes, or written to `path` (then the path is returned).

Google Docs, Sheets and Slides have no content of their own: pass
`export_as` (`"pdf"`, `"csv"`, `"xlsx"`, `"docx"`, `"pptx"`,
`"txt"`, `"html"` or a MIME type) to download them converted (Drive
exports up to 10 MB). The content is held in memory. For example:

```python
data = google_drive.download(file_id)
google_drive.download(sheet_file_id, "/tmp/sheet.csv", export_as="csv")
```

### share_link

```python
google_drive.share_link(file_id, *, role='reader', connection=None)
```

Let anyone with the link open the file (as `role`) and return the link.

`role` is `"reader"`, `"commenter"` or `"writer"`. The file isn't
listed publicly: only people with the link find it. A shared drive or an
organisation may forbid link sharing (FORBIDDEN). For example:

```python
link = google_drive.share_link(uploaded["id"])
```

### client

```python
google_drive.client(connection=None, *, timeout=30)
```

The shared client of `connection`, for calls this module has no function for.

Paths are relative to `https://www.googleapis.com`. For example:

```python
about = google_drive.client().get("/drive/v3/about", params={"fields": "storageQuota"})
```

## Errors

Every function raises `pyrunner_integrations.IntegrationError` (a `pyrunner_connections.ConnectionsError`, so one `except` catches both) with `code`, `status` (the HTTP status, or None) and `retry_after` (seconds, or None). Its message never holds the connection's credentials. Before raising, the client retries a 429 (or a 503 with Retry-After) up to 3 times, waiting what the service asks (up to 60 s; longer, and the error says it in `retry_after`) or else 1, 2 or 4 seconds; other 5xx replies and lost connections only for GET, PUT, DELETE and other calls that are safe to repeat. After a 401 it asks PyRun once for new credentials (an OAuth token is refreshed then) and tries again.

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | The service refused the request as malformed (HTTP 400, 405 or 422). |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | The service refused the credentials (HTTP 401), also after PyRun was asked for new ones. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | The account may not do this (HTTP 403): a missing scope or permission. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | No such thing (HTTP 404 or 410). |
| `CONFLICT` | It clashes with the current state (HTTP 409 or 412). |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Too many requests (HTTP 429), still after the retries; `retry_after` says when to try again. |
| `HTTP_ERROR` | Any other 4xx reply. |
| `SERVER_ERROR` | The service failed (HTTP 5xx), still after the retries. |
| `UNREACHABLE` | The service couldn't be reached (DNS, refused connection, TLS). |
| `TIMEOUT` | No reply in time. |
| `BAD_RESPONSE` | A reply that can't be used: broken JSON, too many redirects or pages, a repeated page cursor. |
| `NOT_HTTP` | The connection isn't an HTTP connection (an SMTP login). |
| `CONNECTION_...` | The connection can't be used: `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `CONNECTION_EXPIRED`... (see [Connections](../run-context.md#connections)). |
